nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-01.prompt: The circumference of a circle is $a\pi$ centimeters and the area of the same circle is $4a\pi$ square centimeters, where $a>0$. Compute the numerical value of $a$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-02.prompt: The European research department at the United Nations employs $30$ people, all of whom speak French, Italian, or Spanish. Five of them speak all three languages. Nine speak French and Spanish. Twenty speak Italian, of which $12$ also speak French. Eighteen speak Spanish. No one speaks only French. Compute how many speak only Spanish.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-03.prompt: The diagram shows trapezoid $ABCD$ with $\overline{AB}\perp\overline{AD}$, $\overline{CD}\perp\overline{AD}$, $\angle ABD=45^\circ$, and $CD=AB+6$. If the area of the trapezoid is $88$ square inches, compute the length of $\overline{AB}$ in inches.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-04.prompt:
For $x>0$, compute all ordered triples of **integers** $(x,y,z)$ that satisfy the following system of equations:
$$\begin{aligned}x+y+z&=9\\ z^x&=y^{2x}\\ 3^z&=3\cdot3^x\end{aligned}$$

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-05.prompt: Write the sum $\sqrt{\frac74+\sqrt3}+\sqrt{\frac74-\sqrt3}$ as an integer in simplest form.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-07.prompt: If the length of the edges of a given cube were increased by $1$ inch, the volume would increase by $217$ cubic inches. Compute the length, in inches, of an edge of the cube.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-08.prompt: Homer and Ned agreed to play a game. If heads appeared on the toss of an ordinary coin, Ned had to double the amount of money that Homer had. If the result was tails, then Homer had to pay Ned \$24. As it turned out, the coin came up heads, tails, heads, tails, heads, and then tails. After this series of tosses, Homer ended the game with exactly zero dollars (not owing Ned any money). Compute how much money Homer started with (in dollars).

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-09.prompt: The diagram shows square $ABCD$ with diagonal $\overline{AC}$. $\overline{BE}$ and $\overline{BF}$ trisect $\angle ABC$, and $\overline{EG}$ and $\overline{EH}$ trisect $\angle AEB$. Compute the ratio of the measure of $\angle EGH$ to the measure of $\angle EHG$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-10.prompt: The nonzero three-digit base $9$ number $\underline{ABC}_9$ is equal to the three-digit base $7$ number $\underline{CBA}_7$. If $A$, $B$ and $C$ each represent a single digit, compute the value of this number in base $10$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-11.prompt: The line $x+2y=8$ intersects the $x$- and $y$-axes at the points $A$ and $B$ respectively. Point $C$ is on line segment $\overline{AB}$ such that $BC:CA=3:1$. A line drawn through $C$ perpendicular to $\overline{AB}$ intersects the $x$-axis at the point $(t,0)$. Compute the value of $t$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-12.prompt: Compute the sum, in degrees, of all of the values of $x$, where $0^\circ\le x<360^\circ$, such that $\sin(60^\circ+x)=2\sin x$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-14.prompt: Compute the area of the triangle whose vertices are the center and $y$-intercepts of the circle $x^2-6x+y^2+12y+20=0$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-15.prompt: Compute all real solutions of the equation $|x+2|=2\cdot|x-2|$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-16.prompt: Compute the number of ordered pairs $(X,Y)$, with $X<Y$, such that the three distinct natural numbers $21$, $X$, and $Y$ have a greatest common factor of $21$ and a least common multiple of $462$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-18.prompt: The diagram shows three congruent circles, each tangent to the other two. The circles are circumscribed by an equilateral triangle. If the area of the triangle is $96+64\sqrt3$, compute the area of one of the circles.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-19.prompt: The points $(0,2)$, $(1,3)$ and $(2,2010)$ all lie on the graph of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$. Compute the ordered triple $(a,b,c)$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-20.prompt: A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. Circle $A$ is circumscribed about the square and circle $B$ is circumscribed about the equilateral triangle. Compute the ratio of the area of circle $A$ to the area of circle $B$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-21.prompt: Let $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Define a sequence where $a_1=2$ and $a_n=\begin{cases}a_{n-1}+i, & \text{if } n \text{ is even}\\ i\cdot a_{n-1}, & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}\end{cases}$. Compute the value of the next term (after $a_1$) which is a real number.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-22.prompt: Let $ABCDEFGH$ be a regular octagon. If the area of the octagon is $8$, compute the area of rectangle $ABEF$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-23.prompt: If Mary drives to work at an average speed of $40$ miles per hour, she will arrive late by $1$ minute. If she starts at the same time and drives the same route to work averaging $45$ mph, she will arrive $1$ minute early. Compute the distance in miles that Mary drives to work.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-24.prompt: Compute the sum of all two-digit numbers which have the property that the number equals seven more than the sum of the squares of its digits.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-26.prompt: Consider the linear function $f(x)=ax+b$. Compute all ordered pairs $(a,b)$ such that for all real numbers $x$, $f(f(x))+f(x)=6x+60$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-27.prompt: In the diagram below, $\overline{AD}\perp\overline{BD}$, $CD=18$, $AE=5$, and $CE=8$. Compute the circumference of the circle.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-28.prompt: Define $r$ and $s$ to be the two roots of the equation $x^2-5x+9=0$, and let the equation $ax^2-bx+c=0$ have roots $r+\frac1s$ and $s+\frac1r$. If $a$, $b$ and $c$ are relatively prime whole numbers, compute the ordered triple $(a,b,c)$.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-29.prompt: Compute the number of non-congruent isosceles triangles with a perimeter of $111$ centimeters and all sides of integer length.

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-30.prompt: Compute the number of three-digit numbers with three distinct digits in increasing or decreasing order. Only consider numbers whose leading digit is not zero.
